newsitem.title: INDIA: India government securities edge up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: India government securities edge up in quiet trade.

text.p: Indian government securities were slightly up in quiet afternoon trade Monday, dealers said.
They said the market was quiet as call money rates remained above 5.5 percent and trade will pick up if rates drop below 5.0 percent.
Government securities rose sharply last month driven by demand funded by call money rates below 2.0 percent.
"Prices don't look like falling but I think any fresh rise will be only after call drops below 5.0 percent," said a dealer.
Call money was quoted around 5.5 percent in latest deals against Saturday's close of 5.75-6.25 percent.
In latest deals, the 12.59 percent 2004 stock was traded at 106 rupees against its previous close of 105.9 while the 13.40 percent 2002 rose to 108.75 from 108.60.
